policy: Retain one identity-stable main blade. Non-main blades fund tribute first. Early sell at most one low-grade support per day for a visible upgrade, leaving another support. Banked tribute permits up to six normal growth hits and safe Frenzy on the main blade. Current visible utility governs purchases and explicit replacements. Exhaust affordable merchant restocks; take a survivable miss before delivering the main blade, and deliver it only at otherwise-fatal anger2 when it covers quota. No future RNG inspection.
policy_limits: One hand-authored strategy and this small common-seed sample are an exploratory command probe, not player win-rate or calibrated balance.
Slots4/8 are pre-unlocked entitlement cohorts, not natural rewarded-slot unlock behavior or its time cost.

Ward treatment simulates one verified-earned test callback at the first legal merchant visit, not an SDK/video/ad conversion test. Inventory wards are fungible; individual free-ward causality is not inferred.
Fresh profiles; original permanent unlocks earned only within this one contract. No carry-over unlock population is modeled.
No post-start injected money, probability, relics, levels, swords or skipped rounds; all accepted actions use Session commands and a memory SaveStore.
Exact cooldown pacing models continuous legal input and frozen menu time, without human reaction, watch time, device latency or native persistence failures.
Fixed main-role choice, growth risk limits and credit/merchant rules are imperfect. This tests a second declared loop, not a solver, calibrated player model or game impossibility proof.
The probe stops after the natural21-day ending; extension mastery and full population retention/monetization are untested.
Censored guards and command errors are separate outcomes and are never relabeled natural failures. No automatic balance changes are made.
pilot_note: One-seed/six-cohort availability pilot checks actual trades, replacements and main retention before the fixed twenty-seed sample. Actor constants are frozen before reading pilot outcomes; no outcome-based game or actor tuning.

baseline_reference.note: The strategies change several actor choices, so between-policy outcomes are not a single-factor causal estimate.

delivery_rule.operational_definition: Main identity remains until actual break, final delivery, or terminal retirement. Before main delivery the actor has no remaining non-main sword and no affordable merchant sword route, cannot survive another underpayment without consuming an owned original pardon, and the current main+scrap value covers quota. It does not claim to prove the absence of every future random-proc route.
delivery_rule.main_records_semantics: Each identity has adoption, peak grade/value, growth/safe/emergency hit counts, retained settlement count and end kind. A retained settlement count includes the final settlement if the sword is not delivered; terminal retirement does not mean the blade broke.

ward_comparator: Free per-contract earned ward off/on. Original paid merchant wards stay available in both arms; the free grant uses only the test-earned verifier and is manually armed.

interpretation.conclusion: A second fixed policy activates legal credits, actual small-shelf replacements and retained main-blade banking, and naturally reaches the21-day ending in four controlled cohort paths. This is closure/coverage evidence, not a player win-rate estimate or a validated balance target.
interpretation.cohort_observations: The2-slot arms each finish0/20; the4-slot arms each1/20; the8-slot arms each1/20. Arms share twenty seeds, so the120 paths are correlated and must not be pooled as120 independent players.
interpretation.credit_loop: Mean actual trades increase from the first policy0.75/1.45/1.65 to3.3/6.45/about9.6-9.8 for2/4/8 slots. Mean peak equipped relic count is2/4/7.6. Every2-slot sample uses a real replacement command, so the smaller-shelf loop is exercised rather than bypassed.
interpretation.completion_semantics: The four clears correspond to two common seeds repeated in the ward arms. They finish at anger2 with18 fully paid orders, three underpayments and one purchased original oblivion item; original day21 survival completes the contract. Do not describe them as paying all21 orders.
interpretation.limits: The policy changes early risk allocation, relic priorities, main banking, strategic missed payments and emergency restocking together. It is one declared actor, not a strategy optimizer, real player model, native mobile test or formal guarantee. Main delivery uses visible material/merchant and anger checks, without peeking at outcome RNG or proving all stochastic future paths impossible.
interpretation.no_tuning: No game code/data/numerical parameters changed between policies. Actor constants and source hashes stayed fixed from pilot through formal sample. No further sample expansion or outcome-based parameter changes are made.
interpretation.next_step: Use the concrete legal clear traces and source checks as implementation evidence; separately assess first-time2-slot human play, readability, repeated-contract original unlocks and actual ad behavior before choosing balance or commercial targets.
